Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/23000
Crypto-theft coding convention used throughout this batch: stolen funds coded as confidentiality data variety Virtual currency (data_victim Victim organization unless customer wallets were drained), integrity Fraudulent transaction for the unauthorized transfers, and the USD loss in impact (Asset and fraud). Template Misuse-prt-privabuse followed: actor partner (CMDSS, the USMS custody contractor, NAICS 541512), misuse Privilege abuse of custody access. Caveat: the alleged thief is the son of CMDSS's executive, and whether he formally worked for CMDSS is not stated; partner orientation follows the tag and ZachXBT's view that the theft was only possible through CMDSS's custodial access.
Victim: U.S. Marshals Service (NAICS 922120, issue tag 92 Federal), government Federal, headcount 1001 to 10000 (about 5,000+ staff). Asset S - Other (government custody wallets). Cloud Other (blockchain).
Data/impact: more than $40M alleged in total; on-chain, ~$20M drained Oct 2024 with ~$700K not returned. Impact uses $40M as alleged; reviewer may lower it. Allegations are ZachXBT's and not charged at the time of the articles -> security_incident Confirmed (funds demonstrably moved) but confidence Medium.
Discovery external Security researcher (ZachXBT). Timeline: Oct 2024 drain -> incident 2024-10, dbir_year 2025 by the Nov 1 rule even though it was disclosed in Jan 2026.

event_chain.summary: Custody access abused to drain seized-crypto wallets

summary: Blockchain investigator ZachXBT alleged in January 2026 that John Daghita, son of the head of Command Services & Support (CMDSS), a Virginia IT contractor hired by the U.S. Marshals Service in October 2024 to manage and dispose of complex seized cryptocurrency, stole more than $40 million from wallets holding government-seized crypto. On-chain data shows about $20 million drained from USMS-controlled wallets in October 2024; most was returned within 24 hours but about $700,000 disappeared. The theft surfaced after a leaked Telegram recording showed Daghita moving funds from wallets linked to the seizures.
